_source: Generated by scripts/stage/build_stage_reference.py from harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c29, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c30, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c31 (training runs only). Per stage: active failures = kinds in >= 2 runs of the latest round; policy = kinds that were common earlier and fell to <= 25% of their peak. Regenerated, never appended.

surfaced_not_opened._why: Run fact for the critic: entities that appeared in the agent's search results but were never opened. Shown only at the stages whose most common errors include 'surfaced-not-opened' in the training catalog; disabled if no stage has it.
show_at_stages: Screen candidate matters by reading documents
Read a chosen matter's documents in depth
Search within a candidate matter's files

List files in the document store.purpose: Get an overview of the whole document store by listing its files so later steps know what material exists and where it sits.
List files in the document store.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, before reading or searching specific documents, to see what files are in the store.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran one glob over the whole store to list every file, then used the result to choose what to open.
Ran a whole-store glob in parallel with narrower globs by document type, and treated an empty result as meaningful rather than an error.
List files in the document store.expected_activity: Getting an overview of the whole store: listing all files (often silently capped at ~100 files from a few matters), or `ls`/`find … \
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

List matter folders.purpose: Get an unfiltered overview of the matter folders in the store, by name or by file count, so later stages know what exists and how it is organized.
List matter folders.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, or whenever you need to know which matter folders exist, how many there are, or how many files each holds, before any keyword-based searching.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a shell directory listing of the matters root, counted the folders, and printed the first and last 20-30 names to confirm the full range without flooding output.
When a glob on the matters folder returned nothing, switched to a shell listing, which gave the folder count and the names, and wrote the full list to a scratch file for later reference.
List matter folders.expected_activity: Listing matter folder names (or counting files per folder) across the store, without keyword filtering
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Search file contents for request keyword.purpose: Search the contents of the document store for keywords from the request to surface the candidate matters and files that later steps will open.
Search file contents for request keyword.when_to_use: Use right after the request is understood, typically in parallel with a whole-store file listing, whenever the relevant matters are not already identified by name.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a whole-store glob in parallel with a files-with-matches grep for the request keywords or party names, then used the hit list to choose which matters to open.
After email-heavy grep hits, ran a separate document grep or a recursive shell grep over the store, and also searched file names for topic words to find matters the content grep missed.
Search file contents for request keyword.expected_activity: Running the grep tool (or bash grep -r) over the store for words from the request; often paired with a whole-store glob in the same parallel call
policy: Never rely on a single content grep: if it returns nothing, only reaches email text, or gives a capped or broad hit list, retry with other wording, search file names, list matter folders, and scan .docx text by extraction so document-only evidence and sibling matters surface.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Scan document text with an extraction sc.purpose: Use a script to unzip documents and regex-search their text across the store or a range of matters, to find the matters and files relevant to the request.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.when_to_use: Use when path or file-name listings alone cannot show which matters match the request and document text must be searched for key terms, names or amounts across many matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran four to five parallel scripts over matter-number ranges, each printing per-matter hit counts for strong terms, so a timeout in one range did not lose the whole scan.
Unzipped documents and emails in a threaded scan for the client name and listed only the files and matters with hits, keeping output compact.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.expected_activity: Writing a Python/shell script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store (or a range of matters); prone to 60 s timeouts and very large outputs
policy: Treat every matter surfaced by any scan or listing as a candidate to open, and do not narrow to hand-picked, highest-numbered or executed-named subsets without checking the rest.
failure_patterns: Scans that timed out, ran on partial ranges, matched too narrow a phrase or name, or were limited to certain file names silently missed qualifying matters, and the agent built its candidates from that incomplete output without checking coverage or rerunning.
Scripts printed every hit snippet with no cap across the store, producing millions of characters that filled the context and ended the run before any answer was written.

The agent narrowed its candidate pool using extra required terms, file-name patterns, exact phrases, or truncated output, which dropped matters that the broader scan had already reached and so were never opened.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.passing_runs: Passing runs kept scan output bounded, often printing per-matter hit counts or file lists instead of snippets, and split work into parallel range scripts. They accepted partial output only as a lead and went on to read the matters it reached.

Search file names for request keywords.purpose: Find candidate matters by matching request keywords against file and folder paths across the store, so the set of relevant matters is identified before they are opened.
Search file names for request keywords.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task that needs to locate matters across a store of many matter folders, whenever request keywords could appear in file or folder names.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran find | grep over file paths for request keywords, then a second pass over folder names for document-type words to catch other matters.
Ran a per-matter script matching file names against request words across all matters, then listed a candidate matter's files to confirm.
Search file names for request keywords.expected_activity: Matching request words against file or folder paths
policy: Run file-name searches uncapped or paged to the end, and supplement them with a store-wide content search; if a search is cut off, times out or returns nothing, rerun it narrower or in chunks and try other document-name variants before fixing the candidate set.
failure_patterns: The agent narrowed candidates with a restrictive file-name filter or path regex (such as decisive document names or a fixed naming pattern) that dropped matters whose documents are named differently, even though earlier broad scans had surfaced them, so those matters were never opened.
Search file names for request keywords.passing_runs: Passing runs used several broad path and folder-name searches with varied request words, counted hits per matter, and listed candidate matters in full rather than relying on one narrow name pattern.

Search file names for a document type.purpose: Use file and folder path names across the store, matched against document-type or folder-type words the request does not itself use, to map which matters likely contain the relevant documents, typically as a per-matter listing.
Search file names for a document type.when_to_use: When the request is about a kind of matter or event but the store is organized by matter folders, so file-name words for engagement, agreement, offering, pleading or similar document types must serve as a stand-in to find candidate matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a store-wide path search for several document-type words (agreements, offering papers, term sheets, pleadings), grouped hits per matter, then compared the count against the full matter-folder listing to see which matters were missed.
Listed engagement, opening and intake files for every matter, sampled text from them, and counted matters per prefix to confirm full coverage before moving on.
Search file names for a document type.expected_activity: Matching file or folder paths across the store against document-type or folder-type words that the request itself does not use (e.g. engagement-letter files, transaction-document or pleadings folders), as a stand-in for what the request asks about; often a per-matter listing of such files
policy: Treat file-name pattern hits as a starting map, not the final candidate set: keep matters whose names do not match the pattern, cross-check against broader scans and folder listings, and open or read content before excluding any matter.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

List files in candidate matters.purpose: Enumerate the full file contents of each candidate matter folder under consideration, or find a folder's real path, so the agent can judge which matters actually contain the needed documents.
List files in candidate matters.when_to_use: Use when searches, scans or metadata have surfaced candidate matters and you need to see their actual files, or when a folder path is missing or returns file-not-found.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran one shell loop that listed all files for every matter surfaced by the grep or path-search hits, so none of the hit matters were skipped.
After a file-not-found error, used find or glob to locate the matter's real subfolder, then listed its files.
List files in candidate matters.expected_activity: Listing every file in one or more specific matter folders the agent is considering, or locating a folder's real path
failure_patterns: Matters that clearly qualified surfaced in the agent's own scans, searches or tables, yet it listed and read only a subset of other candidates, so the surfaced qualifying matters were never listed or opened.
List files in candidate matters.passing_runs: Passing runs listed all files for every candidate that surfaced from a search, grep or filename hit, often in one shell loop covering several matters, and re-listed or located the real path when a listing failed, rather than screening matters out by name alone.

Read documents picked from the file list.purpose: To open and read documents selected from the store's file listing when no keyword-search lead points to them, so the agent can gather the matter content it needs.
Read documents picked from the file list.when_to_use: Use when the task concerns a matter visible at the top of the listing and you need to read its memos, agreements, filings, emails or engagement letters directly, without a keyword lead.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read several documents (memos, filings, emails, engagement letters) from the matter at the top of the listing in one batch.

Read a batch from the top matter, then opened engagement letters from several other listed matters with different number prefixes to widen coverage; failed reads on guessed or folder paths were simply retried differently.
Read documents picked from the file list.expected_activity: Opening documents chosen from the (partial) store listing with no keyword-search lead behind the choice
policy: Never treat a capped or partial listing as the whole store: before concluding anything about what exists or qualifies, run keyword or store-wide searches, or sample other matters across different prefixes, so that matters outside the top of the listing surface.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Screen candidate matters by reading docu.purpose: Open and read the opening sections of key documents from the candidate matters surfaced by searches and listings, so each matter can be judged as fitting or not fitting the request on evidence.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.when_to_use: Use after scans, path searches or listings have produced a set of candidate matters and you must confirm each one's fit and role by reading its documents before answering.
examples_from_successful_runs: Took the matters with the most specific grep hits and read their emails, memos and status trackers, so each surfaced candidate was opened.
Listed one candidate's files, read the key court or closing documents there, and re-read the real path when a guessed one failed.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.expected_activity: Reading the opening part of documents (engagement letters, memos, filings) from several candidate matters to judge whether each fits the request
policy: Make sure the proof document for every candidate matter shows up in a search or folder listing before reading, and list each kept matter's folder rather than relying on a transmittal letter, memo or draft.
Count every matter and number series fully from the complete listings and check each one before ranking; do not narrow verification to a subset.
failure_patterns: Matters that appeared in the agent's own scans, filtered lists or file-name searches as qualifying candidates were left out when it chose what to read, so they were never opened and were missing from or wrongly handled in the answer.

The agent listed a matter's folder and saw the proof document (closing memo, executed agreement, carry agreement, motion, rider), but read other documents of that matter instead and never opened or cited the proof document.
The agent opened a candidate using a guessed or copied document path, got file-not-found, and dropped the matter instead of listing the folder and retrying with the real path.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.passing_runs: Passing runs read documents from every matter with the most specific scan hits, listed a candidate's folder before reading, and tolerated a failed guessed path by retrying from the listing. They chose reads from the scan output rather than a hand-picked shortlist.

Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.purpose: Open and read the key documents of the matters already settled on, to extract the specific details and supporting records needed to answer.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.when_to_use: Use after the candidate matters have been narrowed down and you need the executed agreements, closing papers, memos, orders and correspondence of those matters to confirm details.
examples_from_successful_runs: List the chosen matter's folder in full, then read the executed agreement, its exhibits, the closing memo and certificates, and the review memo, rather than only drafts.
Read at least one document from each surfaced candidate, and when a guessed path fails, list the folder or use find to recover the real path.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.expected_activity: Reading further sections/documents of the matter(s) the agent has settled on, to extract details and supporting documents
failure_patterns: A matter that appeared as a candidate in the agent's own search or scan output (with relevant hits) was never opened, because reads went to other matters, so the most relevant or most recent record was missed.

Documents listed or hit in the agent's own directory listings or scan results, such as the executed agreement, closing memo or status memo, were skipped in favour of drafts, redlines, transmittals or other papers, so the answer rested on secondary documents.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.passing_runs: Passing runs opened the executed agreement, closing memo or outcome memo of the matter they picked, often after listing the matter's folder, and covered each surfaced candidate with at least one read before ruling it in or out.

Search within a candidate matter's files.purpose: Run targeted grep or snippet extraction inside a single candidate matter folder or document to confirm facts and pull the passages that support the answer.
Search within a candidate matter's files.when_to_use: Use after candidate matters have been identified and you need to read or extract text from specific matters or documents to verify relevance and gather evidence.
examples_from_successful_runs: Listed a candidate matter's files, then ran a capped snippet script over its executed agreement for the operative clauses and read further at offsets.
Ran parallel capped extraction scripts over all named candidate matters, with sanity checks reporting hit counts per matter and a path check when a script printed nothing.
Search within a candidate matter's files.expected_activity: Grep or snippet extraction restricted to one matter folder or one document
policy: Cap every extraction script's output (per-hit window, hits per file, total characters) and run it over a few matters at a time, so results never fill the context.

If a grep or snippet script returns nothing or only partial hits, list the matter's folder and open the relevant files directly, and run a sanity check with per-matter hit counts before concluding there is nothing.
When a matter is selected, open its primary documents (executed agreement, complaint, indenture) that appeared in the listings rather than substituting side correspondence or post-closing memos.
failure_patterns: Matters or executed agreements that the earlier path search or scan output had already surfaced were left out of the hand-picked candidate list for the extraction scripts, so they were never opened and were missing from the answer.
Search within a candidate matter's files.passing_runs: Passing runs built the candidate set from everything the scans surfaced rather than a hand-picked subset, ran capped scripts over all of them, and reported per-matter hit counts so that matters with no hits were noticed and checked.

Tabulate candidate matters from saved re.purpose: Turn the scan and search outputs saved by earlier steps into per-matter counts, rankings, filtered or merged hit lists and coverage checks, so that the right candidate matters go forward for reading, without re-reading any documents.
Tabulate candidate matters from saved re.when_to_use: Use after scans or searches have saved their hits to scratch files and you must count, rank, filter, merge or check coverage of those hits against the matter-folder list before choosing which matters to read.
examples_from_successful_runs: Compared the matters in the raw scan outputs with the narrower filtered list, saved the union, and listed the matters the filter had excluded along with their snippets.
Checked each saved range file's scanned-matter count against the folder list, found the matters missing from the outputs, then merged per-matter hit counts across all files.
Tabulate candidate matters from saved re.expected_activity: Working only from scratch files saved by earlier steps, without extracting document text again or reading documents: per-matter counts, rankings or tables of saved scan or search hits; filters, unions or intersections of hit lists; printing the saved hits of chosen matters; coverage checks of the saved output against the matter-folder list; or a hand-written per-matter table of findings already read. A folder-name list for a coverage check may accompany it; a span that also walks matter folders for file names is tagged `mixed intents`. Rarely a stage with no tool call whose summary ranks candidates already read
failure_patterns: The filter applied to the saved hits was too narrow (file-name patterns, document-type words, or a partial printout of the aggregate), so matters whose qualifying hits were in document text or in differently named files were dropped and never reached the reading list.
Tabulate candidate matters from saved re.passing_runs: Passing runs built candidate sets from the full saved output by merging or taking unions of the scan files, and compared the raw matter set with the filtered one. They also checked per-file matter counts and coverage against the folder list, and used inclusive exact-phrase filters that printed snippets rather than relying on file-name filters.

Calculate figures for the answer.purpose: Run a short script over figures already read to compute the values the deliverable needs, such as counts, distributions, day counts, averages or rates, without querying the document store.
Calculate figures for the answer.when_to_use: Use after the source data has been read or saved (for example a folder list or scan file) and the answer needs derived counts or rates, with a stage open for the work.
examples_from_successful_runs: Counted items per category from a saved folder list or scan file, covering every folder and not only the leading categories, and kept the item identifiers alongside the counts for citation.
Ran the calculation under the correct stage label and re-ran it cleanly after a syntax error, so the final figures came from one consistent computation.
Calculate figures for the answer.expected_activity: A short script that computes values for the deliverable (day counts, averages, rates) from figures already read; it does not touch the document store
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Write the response.purpose: Write the final deliverable file that answers the request, naming the right matters with correct identifiers, clients and facts, drawn only from what was actually read and within the requested set.
Write the response.when_to_use: Use once the candidate matters have been gathered and checked, when the answer file (a named matter, a list or count of matters, or a no-match finding with reasons) is ready to be written or overwritten.
examples_from_successful_runs: Wrote two qualifying matters with their key documents, followed by a list of excluded candidates and the reason for each.
Wrote that no matter meets a strict reading of the request and listed the near candidates with why each falls short.
policy: State the matter number from the folder path read, along with title, parties and date, and cite the specific adopted-terms or closing document for each included matter.
Say explicitly that each kept matter closed or was executed, and give the firm-wide conclusion the question asks for rather than narrowing to one client.
Open the surfaced documents and compare candidate matters before writing, never answering from a partial scan output.
failure_patterns: Over-inclusion: the answer counts or lists matters, facilities or deals outside the requested set (other practice groups' matters, planned, terminated or non-qualifying structures, or unopened earlier deals), inflating counts, denominators and buckets.

Under-inclusion: the answer excludes in-scope matters that were read or listed, by applying exclusions the request did not make, judging from snippets or draft markings, or treating closing papers as missing, and sometimes leaving a matter out with no reason.

Misstated facts: the answer attaches the wrong client, matter number, amount, structure or direction (paid versus recovered) to a matter, often from mixed-up parallel read results, thin reads, or an internal number, or misclassifies deal type.
Missing detail: the answer lists a chosen matter's closing papers but omits the key-terms or issues memo it had opened.
Incomplete population: a rate is computed over only the hand-picked or conveniently found deals rather than the whole set of the practice's matters the request covers.
Write the response.passing_runs: Passing runs wrote only matters verified within the requested set, stated exclusions or near candidates with reasons, and said plainly when no matter met every requirement instead of padding the list.

Check or revise the response.purpose: Re-read the written response and verify cited paths and details, making only edits that make it more accurate and better scoped without changing which matters genuinely qualify.
Check or revise the response.when_to_use: Use after the response is drafted and before finishing, to re-read it, confirm every cited file path and detail exists, and tighten the headline, scope and completeness wording.
examples_from_successful_runs: Globs or lists the cited files to confirm each path exists, fixes any wrong path in the response, and re-reads the response afterward.
Re-reads a source document to confirm a cited date or term, then edits the opening or completeness wording to match the reviewed scope without changing the counted matters.
Check or revise the response.expected_activity: Editing the written response, re-reading it, or re-checking a cited path/detail after writing
policy: Do not add non-qualifying or older matters as secondary precedents or inflate the denominator during review; keep the counted set limited to matters that meet the request's criteria on their own documents.
Do not upgrade or reclassify a matter into the qualifying set on the strength of references in other documents or a wider search; confirm against that matter's own documents and terms.
failure_patterns: Edits during review move a matter that does meet the request out of the counted set into a note, lead or exclusion because of a side feature (a different role, a draft-only agreement, a later termination, extra post-closing terms, or a partial read), even though the evidence already read shows it qualifies.
Check or revise the response.passing_runs: Passing runs used the review to verify cited paths and details and to soften or scope headline, completeness and exclusivity wording, rather than reclassifying matters out of the counted set.
